title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated content was used to clone the identity of a real, named attorney. The scammer created fake profiles and a large volume of fabricated videos using that attorney's likeness, then placed social media advertisements making false promises about immigration services. The fraud operated entirely outside any legitimate AI deployment, meaning there was no institutional system to audit, no developer to hold accountable, and no built-in safeguard to fail. The vector was social media advertising, and the deception succeeded because the fabricated material was convincing enough to pass casual inspection.

The failure mode is identity impersonation enabled by synthetic media, combined with social engineering to extract both money and sensitive personal documents. The victim's loss was discovered not by any platform or enforcement mechanism but by a family member's suspicion and a private consultation. Detection required human skepticism applied after the fact, not before. The scale reported, thousands of fraudulent videos and victims across multiple states, suggests the operation ran without meaningful platform intervention for a significant period.

What is not established is who is responsible for creating or distributing the fraudulent content, whether any platform took action, or whether law enforcement has identified a suspect. Reports filed with NYPD and federal agencies are a step in an investigation, not a finding of guilt against any party.

reports.title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A Bronx legal resident from the Dominican Republic lost $4,820 to an immigration scam involving artificial intelligence. Victor Hernandez responded to a social media ad promising citizenship help without taking the official exam, and then sent thousands of dollars through Zelle after being asked repeatedly for personal documents like his Social Security card and residency card. He only discovered the fraud when his wife grew suspicious and they consulted a friend, learning the ad was AI-generated but used the identity of real Miami immigration attorney Angel Leal without his knowledge.

The scammer also attempted extortion after Hernandez realized he had been defrauded. Attorney Leal says his identity has been cloned to create multiple fake profiles and over 8,000 fraudulent videos, affecting victims across the country. He recommends people hire attorneys through in-person meetings rather than social media, and warns that payment requests through cash-sending apps are major red flags. Hernandez filed reports with NYPD and federal law enforcement but now faces financial hardship, falling behind on rent and electricity bills.
